evidence: The structural premises hold: after reading the whole named spec and searching repair/reopen/correct/rebuild/replace/refresh/reset/generation equivalents, it defines no current-generation reopening or correction operation; lines 104–106 permit only the stated closure statuses, and lines 78/110 omit older closed entries from the displayed ledger. However, the finding is not material against the stated scope. Lines 17 and 64 explicitly reuse existing worker-derived resolution, line 72 bounds the guarantee to visibility and citation rather than correct model recognition, and line 76 explicitly assigns semantic closure judgment to the worker and says the daemon cannot prove satisfaction or successful completion. Line 104 reiterates that rule withdrawal meaning is cooperative derived-summary judgment. This is an expressly accepted semantic-correctness limit, with uncertainty guidance to leave items open; the proposal does not promise a repair lifecycle for mistaken worker judgments. Lines 78 and 98 also preserve source messages and old-generation data rather than deleting them. Requiring an additional repair transition would extend this scoped classification/lifetime proposal beyond its inherited resolution contract, not establish a violation of a promised guarantee.
